info.title: Gateway Inference API
info.description: Stable since 1.0.0 (2026-11-06). Within `/api/inference/v1/` the contract changes only compatibly: new endpoints, new optional request fields, new response fields, new SSE event names, and new values of open strings such as `finish_reason` and problem `code`. Clients must ignore response fields and SSE events they do not know. A breaking change ships under a new URL version alongside this one. See the compatibility policy in the reference documentation.

post.description: Stores a JSONL input file for the API key's service account. Needs a key with the inference or embeddings capability, and a configured file store (`batch_store_unavailable` otherwise).

get.summary: A file's content, as uploaded or written

post.description: Validates the whole input file, routes every line by its alias's `chat_batch` or `embeddings_batch` route, and reserves every line at the batch price, for its whole output cap, until the completion window ends plus six hours, in one transaction. Any refused line (`batch_validation_failed`, listing every line) or a budget that cannot hold every line (`quota_exceeded`) refuses the batch with nothing reserved. The batch is admitted against rate limits once; its lines are not counted as requests or concurrent requests. A repeated `Idempotency-Key` returns the batch it created.

get.summary: The service account's batches, newest first

post.description: The batch becomes `cancelling` and each provider job is cancelled; lines that finish first are still settled and returned. A batch already ending or ended is returned as it is.

EndUser.name: Gateway-End-User
EndUser.description: The app's ID for the user this request is for (D-028): 1–256 bytes of UTF-8, no control characters, no leading or trailing whitespace. Send a pseudonymous ID, never an email address. Scoped to the key's service account. Where the service account limits its end users, the request is charged to this user's monthly plan allowance and then their credits, as well as to every other budget; where it requires one, a request without it is 400 `end_user_required`. Takes precedence over the body's `user`.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying a request rejected by a rate or concurrency limit, or by an open provider circuit

Problem403.description: Forbidden, including `end_user_not_registered`: the end user has no plan and the service account no default (D-028); and `routing_policy_denied`: the organization's routing policy permits none of the alias's deployments (D-023).

value.title: Not Found
value.detail: model alias is not available for this operation

Problem429.description: Too Many Requests: a quota is exhausted (`quota_exceeded`), or a rate limit (`rate_limit_exceeded`) or concurrency limit (`concurrency_limit_exceeded`) is reached. Limit rejections carry `Retry-After`. A `quota_exceeded` that carries `end_user` is the end user's allowance and credits (D-028); without it, a budget. A rate or concurrency refusal that carries `end_user` is their plan's `requests_per_minute`, `tokens_per_minute` or `max_concurrent` (named by `limit`); without it, a rate-limit policy of the organization, a team, a service account or the API key, its level named by `scope` and its limit by `limit`. A `tokens_per_minute` limit, of a plan or a policy, may also lower a request's output cap to what fits, as a budget does.

Problem503.description: Service Unavailable. The code `provider_circuit_open` means the deployment has failed repeatedly and requests to it are refused without calling the provider; it carries `Retry-After`.

user.description: The end user, as OpenAI's `user` field; used where `Gateway-End-User` is not sent (D-028).

tools.description: Functions the model may call (D-032). Only a model alias whose every deployment takes tools accepts them; others refuse the request with `tools_unsupported`, never drop them.

parallel_tool_calls.description: `false` asks for at most one call per response. Needs `tools`. Bedrock and Gemini cannot honour `false` and refuse it with `tools_unsupported`.

Message.description: A conversation message. `content` is required except on an assistant message that carries `tool_calls` (D-032), where it may be null or absent. A `tool` message answers one call of the assistant message just before it, by `tool_call_id`; every call is answered before the next non-tool message, and a conversation with calls or results defines `tools`.

tool_calls.description: Assistant messages only: the calls the model made, as a response returned them.

tool_call_id.description: Tool messages only, and required on them: the id of the call this message answers.

user.description: The end user, as OpenAI's `user` field; used where `Gateway-End-User` is not sent (D-028).

errors.description: Batch creation only (`batch_validation_failed`): every refused line of the input file, by line number.

end_user.description: The end user whose own limits refused the request (D-028): with `quota_exceeded`, their allowance and credits cannot cover it; with `rate_limit_exceeded` or `concurrency_limit_exceeded`, their plan's `limit` is reached. Absent when a budget or a rate-limit policy refused it.

allowance_remaining.description: `quota_exceeded` with `end_user`: this period's allowance left, in money units.

limit.description: `rate_limit_exceeded` or `concurrency_limit_exceeded`: which limit is reached, of the end user's plan (with `end_user`) or of the policy at `scope`. `Retry-After` says when the request could fit; a request whose input bound and reasoning allowance, with one output token, are more than a `tokens_per_minute` limit never fits (the detail says so, and `Retry-After` is 60).

scope.description: `rate_limit_exceeded` or `concurrency_limit_exceeded` without `end_user`: the level of the rate-limit policy whose `limit` is reached. Every policy covering a request applies; the one named is the one whose wait is longest, or one the request can never fit.

credit_balance.description: `quota_exceeded` with `end_user`: unspent, unreserved credit, in money units. May be above zero and still not cover the request's largest cost.

currency.description: `quota_exceeded` with `end_user`: the currency of the allowance and credits.

tool_calls.description: The same calls as `message.tool_calls`, flat (`id`, `name`, `arguments`), as 1.0.0 returned them.
The calls the model made (D-032), OpenAI-shaped; absent when it made none. The choice's `finish_reason` is then `tool_calls`.

code.description: Open string: `invalid_json_line`, `invalid_custom_id`, `duplicate_custom_id`, `invalid_method`, `mismatched_url`, `invalid_body`, a single endpoint's bound code, `model_unavailable`, `insufficient_scope`, `routing_policy_denied`, `accounting_bound_exceeded`, `batch_line_too_large`, `too_many_lines`, `empty_file`, `invalid_file_encoding`, and others later.

line.description: 1-based line of the input file; null for the file as a whole.

purpose.description: `batch` for an input file, `batch_output` for a batch's output or error file.

file.description: JSONL, one request a line: `{custom_id, method: "POST", url, body}`, where `url` is the batch's endpoint and `body` is the request that endpoint takes, with `model` a catalog alias. At most 64 MiB and 10,000 lines.

BatchGatewayExtension.description: The gateway's own account of a batch (D-021), on the single-batch read only: how each group of lines runs and at which price, and what the batch has cost so far and still holds. Never part of OpenAI's object; clients that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.

mode.description: Open string: `native` (the provider's batch API) or `emulated` (each line sent as an ordinary request).

price_source.description: Open string: `batch` (the deployment's batch price) or `on_demand` (its ordinary price, for emulated lines).

cost.description: One entry per currency; amounts in different currencies are never summed.

consumed_minor.description: Settled so far, in minor units.

reserved_minor.description: Still held for lines not yet settled, in minor units.

Tool.description: A function the model may call (D-032). Its definition counts toward the request's input bound and is billed as input by the provider.

parameters.description: A JSON Schema for the arguments, whose `type` is `object`. Defaults to an object with no properties. Passed to the provider as it is; providers accept different subsets of JSON Schema.

ToolCall.description: A call the model made to one of the request's tools (D-032).

id.description: Opaque; send it back unchanged as the `tool_call_id` of the result and in the assistant message's `tool_calls`. Some providers' ids carry state the provider needs when the conversation is replayed.

arguments.description: The arguments as a JSON object, serialized. Generated by the model: validate them against the tool's schema before acting on them.

ToolCallRequest.description: A call the model made, sent back in an assistant message's `tool_calls` (D-032); `arguments` must be a JSON object, serialized.

id.description: Opaque; send it back unchanged as the `tool_call_id` of the result and in the assistant message's `tool_calls`. Some providers' ids carry state the provider needs when the conversation is replayed.

arguments.description: The arguments as a JSON object, serialized. Generated by the model: validate them against the tool's schema before acting on them.

ToolChoice.description: Whether the model must call tools: `auto` (the model decides; the default), `none` (it calls none), `required` (it calls at least one), or a named function it must call. Needs `tools`. A provider that cannot honour the choice refuses the request with `tools_unsupported` (Bedrock has no `none`).
